Without a declared target, a detector score could be interpreted as evidence about the initial drafter, the latest editor, the current wording, or simply a stylistic resemblance to its training data.

attempts.text: Binary AI-text detection becomes conceptually unstable when a document has both human and model contributors. Existing studies already evaluate sentence-level hybrid text, paraphrase attacks, same-generator rewriting, human-edited AI drafts, realistic web rewrites, and cross-dataset failures. The unresolved question is therefore not whether detectors fail on edited text, but what their scores track when origin and latest editor vary independently. We propose a bidirectional revision-history audit built from identical briefs and fully logged trajectories: human-origin texts edited by a model and model-origin texts edited by a human, alongside same-origin editing controls. Copy-editing and structural revision will be matched across routes, as will bounded substantive revision and controlled sentence replacement. Human reviewers will verify claim preservation and mark changed spans. Document and sentence detectors will be evaluated against three labels kept separate: original drafter, latest editor, and sentence provenance. Primary analysis will measure within-lineage score movement, false positives on human-origin material, and the extent to which detector outputs correspond to each possible target. The contribution is a process-aware evaluation protocol, not a forensic authorship system or proof of misconduct.

Existing studies already evaluate sentence-level hybrid text, paraphrase attacks, same-generator rewriting, human-edited AI drafts, realistic web rewrites, and cross-dataset failures. The unresolved question is therefore not whether detectors fail on edited text, but what their scores track when origin and latest editor vary independently. We propose a bidirectional revision-history audit built from identical briefs and fully logged trajectories: human-origin texts edited by a model and model-origin texts edited by a human, alongside same-origin editing controls. Across routes, copy-editing, structural revision, bounded substantive revision, and controlled sentence replacement will be matched. Human reviewers will verify claim preservation and mark changed spans. Document and sentence detectors will be evaluated against three labels kept separate: original drafter, latest editor, and sentence provenance. Primary analysis will measure within-lineage score movement, false positives on human-origin material, and the extent to which detector outputs correspond to each possible target. The contribution is a process-aware evaluation protocol, not a forensic authorship system or proof of misconduct.
